blockers.issue: The installation scope cannot be changed after the public connection is created.

claim.text: The installation scope cannot be changed after the public connection is created.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Fill out the form with your connection details, including your redirect URI(s) under the OAuth configuration section and the connection’s installation scope — either Any workspace or Selected workspaces only. This can’t be changed after creation.

blockers.issue: If a page is not shared with the connection, API requests will return an error.
blockers.fix: Manually share the page with the connection using the Add connections option in the page menu.

claims.text: Internal connections are scoped to a single workspace and use a static credential called an internal connection API token.
claims.label: official_docs
claims.evidence_quote: Internal connections are scoped to a single workspace and use a static credential called an internal connection API token. They’re ideal for custom automations and workflows — things like syncing data, sending notifications, or building internal dashboards.

claims.text: Public connections use OAuth 2.0 for authentication.
claims.label: official_docs
claims.evidence_quote: Public connections use OAuth 2.0 for authentication. At creation time, you choose their installation scope: Any workspace (any Notion user can install; Marketplace-eligible) or Selected workspaces only (restricted to workspaces you select; not Marketplace-eligible).

claims.text: Personal access tokens are user-scoped tokens for scripts, CLI workflows, Workers, and tools that should act as one Notion user.
claims.label: official_docs
claims.evidence_quote: Personal access tokens (PATs) are user-scoped tokens for scripts, CLI workflows, Workers, and tools that should act as one Notion user. A PAT uses the creator’s workspace membership and page permissions.

claims.text: A personal access token allows API authentication without OAuth.
claims.label: official_docs
claims.evidence_quote: A personal access token (PAT) lets you authenticate API requests as yourself without setting up a connection or completing an OAuth flow.

claims.text: Public connections use OAuth 2.0 for multi-workspace installation, while internal connections are scoped to a single workspace.
claims.label: official_docs
claims.evidence_quote: A public connection is an OAuth connection that users install into their Notion workspaces. Unlike internal connections, which are scoped to a single workspace with a static token, public connections follow the OAuth 2.0 protocol

claims.text: Use a PAT for personal or developer-owned workflows that one Notion user should own.
